message.content:
Lion (Panthera leo) and zebra (Equus quagga) belong to two different orders—Carnivora and Perissodactyla, respectively.  
Their most recent common ancestor is the last common ancestor of the **Laurasiatheria** clade, a group of placental mammals that split from other placentals roughly 90 million years ago. In other words, the lion and zebra share a common ancestor that was a basal Laurasiatherian mammal living around the late Cretaceous period.
message.reasoning:
The user asks: "What is the common ancestor of lion and zebra?" They want a biological answer. The lion (Panthera leo) and zebra (Equus quagga) are both mammals, but belong to different orders: lions are Carnivora, zebras are Perissodactyla. Their common ancestor would be at the level of the last common ancestor of all placental mammals? Actually, the last common ancestor of Carnivora and Perissodactyla is the last common ancestor of all Laurasiatheria? Let's think: Carnivora is part of the clade Laurasiatheria, which also includes Perissodactyla, Cetartiodactyla, Chiroptera, Eulipotyphla, and others. So the last common ancestor of lion and zebra would be the last common ancestor of Laurasiatheria, which is a group of placental mammals that diverged from other placental mammals around 90 million years ago. But maybe the question expects "the last common ancestor of all mammals" or "the last common ancestor of all placental mammals" or "the last common ancestor of all mammals" depending on context. But the lion and zebra diverged from each other at the order level: lion is in Carnivora, zebra in Perissodactyla. The last common ancestor of those two orders is the last common ancestor of Laurasiatheria. That ancestor would have lived about 90 million years ago. So the answer: the last common ancestor of the Laurasiatheria clade, which is a placental mammal that lived ~90 million years ago. Alternatively, if we want a more specific taxonomic level: the last common ancestor of the orders Carnivora and Perissodactyla. That ancestor would be a member of the clade Laurasiatheria. So the answer: the last common ancestor of Laurasiatheria, a placental mammal that lived about 90 million years ago.

We can mention that the lion and zebra share a common ancestor at the level of the last common ancestor of all placental mammals, but more specifically at the level of Laurasiatheria. So answer accordingly. No tool needed.
